## GOVERNMENT OF ANDHRA PRADESH
ABSTRACT

Prohibition and Excise - Removal of ARET levied additionally on Bars - Increase of MRPs by
Rs. 10/- per bottle across all sizes except certain segments with marginal augmentation
of retailer margin by 1% of MRP - Restoring parity in pricing - Eliminate inconsistencies in
taxation - Orders - Issued.

## REVENUE (EXCISE-II) DEPARTMENT

## G.O.Ms.No.22

Dated:12-01-2026

Read the following:

1. G.O Ms.No.211, Revenue (Excise) Department, Dt. 30.09.2024.
2. G.O Ms.No.213, Revenue (Excise) Department, Dt. 30.09.2024.
3. G.O Ms.No.229, Revenue (Excise) Department, Dt. 15.10.2024.
4. G.O Ms.No.42, Revenue (Excise) Department, Dt. 10.02.2025.
5. From the Director, Excise & Prohibition in C.R.No.4154/2025/CPE/E3,
6. Dated:24-12-2025
7. From the MD, APSBCL, C.R.No.4154/2025/CPE/E3, dated 05.01.2026.

## ORDER:

## @@@

Government have reviewed the Excise policies implemented during the period
2019-24 and prepared the Way Forward regarding the Excise policies to be pursued for the
ensuing Excise years. Pursuant to the Way Forward, a Group of Ministers has been
constituted vide G.O. Rt. No. 582, Revenue (Excise) Dept., Dt: 29.08.2024, for
recommending draft new comprehensive Excise policy on retail trade, pricing of liquor
and taxation and also vide GO Rt. No. 939, Rev (Ex-II) Dept., dated 28-08-2025 to examine
and provide recommendations to the Council of Ministers on all future Excise Policy
proposals. The GoM has met from time to time and made recommendations accordingly.

1. In the reference 1ˢᵗ read above, the Government have issued new Excise Policy with respect to Shops for 2024-26 duly fixing number of Shops, method of disposal, Retail Excise Tax (RET), Retailer’s Margin, etc. As per the orders issued in the reference 2ⁿᵈ read above, the Retailer Margin shall be 20% on the Issue price of IMFL, FL, Beer, Wine and Ready to Drink Varieties.
3. In the reference 3ʳᵈ read above, Government have rationalized the Additional Retail Excise Tax (ARET) on IMFL, FL, Beer, Wine and Ready to Drink varieties supplied to the licensees of Shops, Bars and In-Houses.
5. In the reference 4ᵗʰ read above, Government revised the rates and structure of Additional Retail Excise Tax (ARET-1 and ARET-2) on Indian Made Foreign Liquor, Foreign Liquor and Beer with a view to ensuring stability of prices and sustainability of retail liquor trade.
7. The Group of Ministers met on 22.12.2025 and discussed, among other things, the effects of levy of ARET additionally on liquor products purchased by Bars.
9. The GoM has noted that before November 2019, the invoice price of IMFL and FL supplied by APSBCL wholesale depots was uniform for both Bars and Retail Shops, ensuring parity in the supply and taxation structure. However, from November 2019, Additional Retail Excise Tax (ARET) was additionally levied for the exclusively on IMFL and FL stocks supplied to the bars. This resulted in higher invoice prices for Bars compared to Retail Shops for the same IMFL and FL stocks. Since then, Bars have been paying ARET additionally.
11. The exclusive levy of Additional Retail Excise Tax (ARET) on liquor supplied to Bars since November 2019 has created a pricing anomaly in the excise framework., with Bars paying higher invoice prices than Retail Shops for identical products supplied from APSBCL depots. This differential treatment is inconsistent with the principle of uniformity in States taxation Policy. This distortion has disrupted market equilibrium and encouraged informal practices. Rationalization of Bar ARET to restore parity between Bars and Shops

and eliminate inconsistencies in taxation structure and to promote fairness, transparency,
and legal defensibility.

1. Further, to safeguard State revenues, the GoM has recommended a calibrated
2. upward revision of MRPs by Rs 10/- per bottle across all sizes, except in respect of IMFL
3. with MRP Rs 99 (180 ml), Beer, Wine and RTDs, through revision of existing ARET slabs
4. with a marginal augmentation of retailer margin on IMFL and FL (including IMFL with MRP
5. Rs 99 (180ml), Beer, wine & RTDs) by around 1% of MRP to maintain equity and stability
6. across both the A4 Shop and Bar licensees, while ensuring commercial balance. This
7. calibrated measure will offset the fiscal impact of ARET withdrawal, ensure price parity
8. between trade segments and enhance overall revenue to the State exchequer.
10. Accordingly, In the references 5ᵗʰ and 6ᵗʰ read above, the Director, Excise &
11. Prohibition submitted proposals based on the recommendations of the GoM for removal of
12. the ARET additionally levied on the stocks of IMFL & FL purchased by Bars, while increasing
13. the MRPs of IMFL & FL by Rs 10/- per bottle across all sizes, except in respect of IMFL with
14. MRP Rs 99 (180 ml), Beer, Wine and RTDs, through structural changes in the ARET slabs
15. along with a marginal augmentation of retailer margin on IMFL and FL (including IMFL with
16. MRP Rs 99 (180ml), Beer, wine & RTDs) by around 1% of MRP.
18. The Government after careful examination of the proposal submitted by the
19. Director, Excise & Prohibition, have approved the recommendations of the GoM and
20. hereby order to remove the Additional Retail Excise Tax additionally levied on Bars and
21. to revise the MRPs of IMFL & FL upwardly by Rs 10/- per bottle across all sizes, except in
22. respect of IMFL with MRP Rs 99 (180 ml), Beer, Wine and RTDs, through structural changes
23. in the ARET slabs along with a marginal augmentation of retailer margin by around 1% of
24. MRP across the spectrum of IMFL & FL.
26. The Director, Excise & Prohibition and the Commissioner of Distilleries & Breweries
27. and the Managing Director, A.P. State Beverages Corporation Limited shall submit
28. proposals for implementation of the Government orders through structural changes in the
29. ARET slabs for taking further action in the matter.
31. This order issues with the concurrence of the Finance (FMU-REV) Department vide
32. their U.O. Note No. FIN01-FMU0PC(REV)/163/2025-FMU-REV, Comp No. 2928986
33. Dt:07.01.2026.
